newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks continue record-breaking charge.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks continue record-breaking charge.

text.p: Mexican stocks left initial breath-taking gains far behind in late morning trade on Thursday as foreign bulls continued to flood the market with buy orders, dealers said.
The leading IPC share index was up 112.99 points, or 2.27 percent, at 5,087.22.
"It's sheer joy. Everything is in demand," a floor trader said. "It's like 1987 all over again, when you could hit every ball they pitch at you. You can get whatever you ask for right now."
"They even had to suspend trade in Banacci, it was rising so fast," he added.

Dealers said foreign buyers had been encouraged by the central bank taking steps to prevent the peso from becoming too strong, by raising its month-end dollar put auction to $500 million from $300 million.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had meanwhile softened 3.3 centavos to 7.8190/7.8230 per dollar.

Trading volume of 121.2 million shares was very brisk for mid-session dealing, even after allowing for cross trades totaling 27 million, which dealers said evidenced the strong presence of foreign dealers.
Banacci, one of Mexico's biggest financial groups, had risen 2.25 pesos to 24.05 pesos.
